value: female antennal EAG response to 1 mg DEET did not change in amplitude when the sample was heated to 135 C (t = 0.02, df = 12, P = 0.986); the amplitude itself is not in the quoted sentence
method: electroantennography (EAG) on female antennae with a coupled induction heating system (carbon steel wire heated to 135 C for the sample) against the same dose delivered unheated at room temperature (about 25 C)
conditions: non-blood-fed females 4 to 7 days old, Orlando strain; at least seven antennae per chemical, each from a different female; 1 mg DEET applied in 10 uL acetone; baseline is the unheated sample, values corrected by subtracting the matched blank (acetone-treated paper strip, clean air); the two-group test with df = 12 compares heated and unheated 1 mg; a different dose, 0.1 mg DEET, rose about 3-fold on heating (0.11 to 0.33 mV, P = 0.002) and matched unheated 1 mg, so the null here is for the 1 mg dose only; method paper on delivery of low-volatility compounds, not a sensitivity threshold

source.authors: Yang L, Liu Y, Richoux GM, Bernier UR, Linthicum KJ, Bloomquist JR
